observations.text: SP, on the first exposure to the maneuver, followed the T/O sequence with the IP directing the Lineup Check and performing part of the L/G and flaps retraction. Runway centerline was held to within 12 ft and take off airspeed exceeded the calculated T/O data by 12 knots before the IP prompted the correction. Performance is at the desired MIF for the Training Section but at its lower edge, since the profile could not be flown without IP assistance. Increased familiarity with the calculated T/O data and with the climbing attitude reference is expected to improve independence in the next sortie.

SP executed the T/O sequence without IP intervention on the controls, requiring only verbal prompts for the After Takeoff Checklist and for the acceleration to the standard climb airspeed. Deviations reached 10 ft from the runway centerline and +10 knots on take off airspeed, recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's call. Independence in bringing and maintaining the proper T/O attitude was beyond the level expected at this point of the syllabus. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Lineup Check without omissions, allowed no A/C movement during engine run-up and flew the T/O with no IP prompts. Lateral displacement from the runway centerline reached 8 ft and take off airspeed reached +8 knots over the calculated T/O data, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. L/G and flaps retraction was completed inside the speed limit and the standard climb airspeed was established. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the Lineup Check without omissions, released brakes on the runway centerline and brought the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the calculated speed. Runway centerline was held within 4 ft and take off airspeed within +3 knots of the calculated T/O data, with L/G and flaps retracted inside the speed limit and the standard climb airspeed established without prompting. Accuracy and speed of execution were well above the level expected for this sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the complete T/O sequence, from Lineup Check through After Takeoff Checklist, without omissions and without any IP input. Runway centerline was held within 1 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated T/O data, with the proper climbing attitude captured on the first input and maintained. Configuration clean-up and acceleration to the standard climb airspeed were flown with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a late and shallow rotation input that did not bring the A/C to the proper T/O attitude, allowed the A/C to accelerate on the runway past the calculated rotation speed. Take off airspeed exceeded the calculated T/O data by 15 knots and lateral displacement reached 18 ft from the runway centerline. The IP had to take the controls to correct the drift and to complete the L/G retraction. Review of the T/O attitude reference and of the calculated T/O data is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not execute the Lineup Check without omissions and did not check A/C performance against the calculated T/O data. Take off airspeed was allowed to reach +16 knots over the calculated value and the A/C tracked 20 ft left of the runway centerline. The IP directed the centerline correction and performed the flaps retraction. Restoration of the scan sequence between the runway picture and the airspeed indication is required.

SP completed the T/O within the desired standards for the Training Section, holding the runway centerline within 10 ft and take off airspeed within +10 knots of the calculated T/O data. Both corrections followed the IP's verbal prompts rather than the SP's own recognition, and the After Takeoff Checklist was started only after a reminder. Performance is marginal at the desired MIF, since every deviation sat on the tolerance limit. Earlier self-recognition of the centerline and airspeed trend is expected in the next sortie.

SP executed the Lineup Check without omissions, kept the A/C motionless during engine run-up and flew the whole T/O without IP prompting. Lateral displacement peaked at 8 ft from the runway centerline and take off airspeed at +7 knots over the calculated T/O data, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. The A/C was cleaned up inside the speed limit and the standard climb airspeed was accelerated to and maintained. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Lineup Check and the After Takeoff Checklist without omissions and brought the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the calculated speed. Runway centerline was held within 3 ft and take off airspeed within +2 knots of the calculated T/O data, with L/G and flaps retracted inside the speed limit. The proper climbing attitude was captured accurately and the standard climb airspeed maintained without IP input. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the T/O to a standard well above the level expected at this point of the syllabus, with the Lineup Check and the After Takeoff Checklist completed without omissions and without prompting. Runway centerline was held within 1 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated T/O data through the ground roll and rotation. Configuration clean-up, climbing attitude and acceleration to the standard climb airspeed showed negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to uncoordinated rudder application against the crosswind during the ground roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline after brakes release. Lateral displacement reached 22 ft and take off airspeed was allowed to exceed the calculated T/O data by 13 knots before rotation. The IP intervened on the controls to re-establish the takeoff path and directed the L/G retraction. Directional control technique during the ground roll requires further practice.

SP, due to a lapse in which a briefed item was omitted under workload, did not execute the Lineup Check without omissions and left the flaps setting unverified before brakes release. During the ground roll the A/C reached 24 ft from the runway centerline and take off airspeed exceeded the calculated T/O data by 12 knots. The IP directed the configuration correction and performed part of the After Takeoff Checklist, so the sequence was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to a lookout fixed inside the cockpit that replaced the runway aiming point during the ground roll, did not maintain the A/C at the centerline and did not check A/C performance against the calculated T/O data. Displacement reached 10 ft from the runway centerline and take off airspeed reached +10 knots over the calculated value. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts, with no intervention on the controls.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not execute the T/O with the standard airspeed and did not bring the A/C to the proper climbing attitude at the briefed point. Take off airspeed reached +10 knots over the calculated T/O data and the A/C reached 10 ft from the runway centerline. The IP's verbal prompts were required for both corrections, which were applied with delay. Distribution of attention between the system indication and the takeoff parameters requires improvement.

SP executed the T/O within the desired standards, with the Lineup Check completed without omissions and no A/C movement during engine run-up. Deviations reached 9 ft from the runway centerline and +8 knots on take off airspeed, self-corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention but close to the limit of the tolerance for the Training Section. Performance is marginal at the desired MIF, with the same drift tendency appearing on the ground roll and on the initial climb. Tighter centerline and airspeed control is expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP performed the Lineup Check without omissions, released brakes on the centerline and brought the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the calculated speed. Runway centerline was held within 3 ft and take off airspeed within +3 knots of the calculated T/O data, with L/G and flaps retracted inside the speed limit and the standard climb airspeed established without prompting. Execution was accurate and quick throughout the departure. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the T/O sequence, from Lineup Check to After Takeoff Checklist, without omissions, without prompting and with the A/C held motionless during engine run-up. Runway centerline was held within 1 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated T/O data, and the proper climbing attitude was captured on the first input and maintained. Configuration clean-up and acceleration to the standard climb airspeed showed negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt and excessive back-stick input at rotation that took the A/C past the proper T/O attitude, did not accelerate the A/C to the standard climb airspeed after brakes release. Take off airspeed first fell below the calculated T/O data and then overshot it by 14 knots during the correction, with the A/C 21 ft off the runway centerline. The IP took the controls to re-establish the climbing attitude and completed the L/G and flaps retraction. Rotation rate and attitude capture technique require further instruction.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not maintain the proper climbing attitude once L/G and flaps were selected up. Airspeed decayed below the standard climb airspeed and was then allowed to exceed the calculated T/O data by 13 knots, with the A/C 19 ft off the extended runway centerline. The IP directed the attitude correction and completed the After Takeoff Checklist. The departure could not be flown to the briefed profile without assistance.

SP, due to a trim setting left short of the takeoff position, held a nose-heavy A/C through rotation and did not bring the A/C to the proper T/O attitude at the calculated speed. Take off airspeed reached +10 knots over the calculated T/O data and displacement reached 10 ft from the runway centerline. Both were corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition and without intervention on the controls.

SP, due to a checklist not followed correctly (AE102) before takeoff, omitted two items of the Lineup Check and did not verify A/C performance against the calculated T/O data. During the ground roll the A/C reached 10 ft from the runway centerline and take off airspeed reached +10 knots over the calculated value. Recognition came late and both corrections were made only after the IP's verbal prompts. Checklist discipline before brakes release requires reinforcement.

SP, due to a delayed rudder correction at brakes release, allowed the A/C to move 8 ft off the runway centerline during the first part of the ground roll. Take off airspeed reached +7 knots over the calculated T/O data before the proper climbing attitude was set. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention, and the After Takeoff Checklist was completed without omissions.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, did not check A/C performance against the calculated T/O data during the ground roll. Take off airspeed reached +8 knots over the calculated value and lateral displacement reached 7 ft from the runway centerline. Both were recognized by the SP and corrected in a timely manner without IP prompting, and the standard climb airspeed was then established and maintained.

SP executed the T/O accurately and quickly, holding the runway centerline within 5 ft and take off airspeed within +5 knots of the calculated T/O data, with the Lineup Check and the After Takeoff Checklist completed without omissions. Both values sat at the edge of the tolerance for the Training Section and the proper climbing attitude required a second correction before the standard climb airspeed was maintained. Performance is marginal at the desired MIF. Finer attitude capture at rotation is expected to bring the deviations further inside the standard.

SP executed the complete T/O sequence without omissions, without prompting and with no A/C movement during engine run-up. Runway centerline was held within 1 ft and take off airspeed within +1 knot of the calculated T/O data, with L/G and flaps retracted well inside the speed limit. The proper climbing attitude was captured on the first input and the standard climb airspeed maintained with negligible deviations. Above end of block MIF achieved.
